tagline.text: "Instant life in a foil packet, now immortalized on an unreadable L2 rollup because Harold Hillier wouldn't sign the release."

future_value.text: "Everyone looks at the 1998 mail-order comic book back cover and sees a novelty gag you ordered with allowance money and a self-addressed stamped envelope. But you’re not looking at the biology, chat. You’re looking at decentralized, low-maintenance aquatic civilization delivered straight to your mailbox via USPS bulk mail. Mint number seventy-three isn't just a JPEG of two cartoon shrimp with human teeth; it's a foundational stake in the primordial soup of the digital economy. While the paper hands are crying about liquidity, we’re holding the actual building blocks of life. On the chain. Forever."

collectors_note.text:
A high-contrast, aggressively compressed 48x48 pixel GIF of the classic 1990s comic book ad illustration—two excessively smiling, human-faced aquatic royalty figures wearing golden crowns, swimming triumphantly through what appears to be a glass bowl of murky tap water laced with green algae and unexploded nutrient powder.
The animation consists of exactly four jerky frames where their eyes dilate in terrifying unison while a faint, low-bitrate MIDI file of the Saved by the Bell theme song plays on an infinite loop. It was minted on an abandoned side-chain whose block explorer is currently a dead link to a GeoCities guestbook. It is worth 0 SOVS at every bank, pawn shop, and shady back-alley terminal in Debaucheryville, permanently and by design.

collectors_note.text:
A scratched, unplated aluminum token roughly the shape and weight of a discarded beer bottle cap, bearing a stamped QR code on one face and **MINT #42** on the reverse. It smells permanently and inexplicably of Kahlúa, cheap stale beer, and fresh-cut grass.
Scanning it on the party’s phone loads an expired 2003 Geocities fansite dedicated entirely to top-down country music ringtones, featuring a grey background, a broken-image icon of a cowboy boot, a hit counter reading **000019**, and an unstoppable MIDI loop of a synthetic banjo. The underlying digital asset is an 11-frame looping GIF of a zero-turn mower executing a clean donut on a manicured horse country pasture, complete with a tiny pixelated cowboy hat bouncing slightly out of sync on the seat. It is worth **0 SOVS** at every bank, pawnshop, and back-alley terminal across Sinfonia and Debaucheryville, permanently and by design.

acquisition_story.text: Gifted by Aaron the Unflappable after drunkenly losing to his god-tier pocket kings. Can you FEEL IT?

future_value.text: Generational spectral wealth. The physical containment grid may be sparking, but this token is immutable. Zero utility, maximum nostalgia, infinite yield.

collectors_note.text: Before app-based food delivery, four guys in stained jumpsuits charged municipal governments ten grand to trap gods in a Tupperware container. This asset captures pure, uncut American optimism: the belief that any cosmic nightmare can be solved with unlicensed nuclear reactors and an invoice with net-30 terms.

future_value.text: The original shitcoin. Unbacked, mass-produced, and stored in a Tupperware bin under a basement stairwell. Intrinsic value: $0.04. Market sentiment: Infinite.

collectors_note.text: Before JPEG monkeys, entire suburban economies collapsed because a billionaire named Ty convince the nation that a $5 stuffed frog was a sovereign wealth fund. Millions of college funds were liquidated and converted into acrylic-encased polyester bears with typos on their tags. This item represents the exact moment American finance abandoned math and embraced soft, bean-filled optimism.
